full_judgment: 35. Mr Afric relied on the case of the province of East Pakistan vs Jogesh Chandra Lodh, 11 DLR SC 11 wherein it has been observed that where the officer concerned did not apply his mind to the question the requisition order is invalid. That petition was filed before acquisition, challenging the order of requisition. Similarly case cited by Mr Afric reported in 15 DLR page 453 (Herama Chandra Battacharjee vs The Secretary, Department of Revenue and others the petitioner challenged order of derequisition The citations have got no manner of application in the present case, In the case of Bangladesh vs Nabab Abdul Malik Jute Mills Ltd. reported in 60 DLR(AD) 7 it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division that once the property is acquired and Gazette Notification is published under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of the Property Act; the fight, title and ,interest, if any, of the owners are extinguished and preparation of Khatian and payment of rent does not improve the position of the original owner in respect of acquired land.
